questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and apply it again right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and apply it again right away.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure. Then apply the brake again with slow, controlled pressure.

questions.question: Where is there the greatest danger of conflict between you and other vehicles?

options.text: At an intersection
On the highway
On any road

questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles and other vehicles have the most potential for conflict.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Yes, they have blind spots like cars do.
No, because motorcycles are smaller than cars.
No, mirrors are not required on motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they have blind spots like cars do.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to ride safely:

options.text: Gets better.
Stays the same.
Gets worse.

questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride your motorcycle if you have consumed any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What colors should motorcycle riders wear to be most visible?

options.text: Brown, gold, silver, and white
Blue, black, gray, and purple
Orange, red, yellow, and green

questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green colors. These colors help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: How should you adjust your rearview mirror?

options.text: So you can see the road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
So it does not show any part of your body.
So it only shows the road behind you, not the side lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you can see the road behind and to the side of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirror to see the road behind and to the side of your motorcycle. It is okay if you see the edge of your arm or shoulder.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle for proper control?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit with your arms slightly bent and use them to steer. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.
Stop only if other traffic is coming.
Vehicles are entering the roadway ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all other traffic and pedestrians pass, then proceed when safe.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane to see around vehicles ahead.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front to use their headlights.
Slow down to have more time to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to have more time to avoid unexpected hazards.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your following distance and stay flexible with your lane position.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Drift into another lane of traffic.
Get through the turn faster.
Keep control of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drift into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning or taking a curve.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the left portion of the lane.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: To reduce your crash risk, do all of the following except:

options.text: Use your signals and brake lights to show your intentions.
Wear dark-colored clothing.
Keep enough space ahead of your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, make yourself visible to others. Communicate your intentions, keep a safe space around your motorcycle, watch the road ahead, spot hazards early, and be ready to react.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen:

options.text: At intersections.
On open roads.
In parking lots.

questions.explanation: Most accidents between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the motorcycle rider the right-of-way.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear all of the following except:

options.text: A DOT-approved helmet.
A leather jacket.
A sweatshirt.

questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects you from injuries.

questions.question: __________ can cause motorcycle accidents.

options.text: Following too closely
Using your horn incorrectly
Talking to other drivers

questions.explanation: Following too closely (tailgating) is a major cause of motorcycle accidents. Always keep a safe distance when riding behind another vehicle.

questions.question: To help other drivers see your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight.
Weave back and forth in your lane.
Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to make your motorcycle visible to other drivers. Check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, ride in:

options.text: The left portion of your lane.
The center portion of your lane.
The right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Staying on the side nearest the passing driver is dangerous. Staying on the far side may encourage them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding __________, you face the greatest risk of conflict with other vehicles.

options.text: On the expressway
Near an intersection
In a group

questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. When approaching an intersection, position yourself where other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When you are stopped, you should:

options.text: Stay in first gear.
Stay in neutral.
Stay in second gear.

questions.explanation: Stay in first gear when stopped. This lets you quickly move away if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What gear should your motorcycle be in when you start the engine?

options.text: First gear.
Neutral.
Third gear.

questions.explanation: Always put your motorcycle in neutral before you start the engine. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the dashboard that turns on when the engine is on and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: You should hold yourself up with your arms.
Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
You should have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Your elbows should be slightly bent when you grip the handlebars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow traffic light means the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can. If you are already in the intersection, keep going.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection?

options.text: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line before moving forward to improve their view of cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop line first. Then slowly move forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward to look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes. Check if anything is coming. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while you look.
